title: Check, include and test: proving your design works

say: Check, include and test: proving your design works.
This is the video for module 3 of UX Design Fundamentals.
In this module you learn to find what is wrong before real users suffer it.
First, a quick expert review against Jakob Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics, which are rules of thumb.

panel.heading: Three ways to find problems
items: Review the design against Nielsen's 10 heuristics
Make it accessible and honest
Watch 5 real users try it
Measure the results and fix the worst first

say: Second, checks so people with weaker eyesight, less schooling or older phones can use it, and so nothing tricks them.

say: Here are five of the ten. Visibility of system status: always tell her what is happening, quickly.

panel.heading: Five heuristics you will use often
items: Show status: Processing, then Successful
Use her words: Buy airtime, not VTU top-up
Give exits: Cancel before final payment
Prevent errors: show the account name first
Plain errors that say what to do next

say: Match the real world. Say buy airtime, not purchase VTU top-up.

say: Choose one task, then go through it twice: once to understand the flow, once to hunt for problems.

panel.heading: Running a heuristic review
items: Choose one task to review
Go through it screen by screen, twice
Note screen, problem, heuristic, fix
Rate each problem from 0 to 4
Combine lists from 2 or 3 reviewers

say: For example, Ngozi reviews a school fees page used by parents in Port Harcourt. After tapping pay, the screen stays blank for up to 30 seconds. That breaks visibility of system status, and parents might pay twice.

say: She rates it 4, a catastrophe. A confusing menu word gets 2. Two colours for one Next button gets 1.
She recommends fixing the worst problems before the next term's payments open.

say: Different reviewers find different problems, so combine lists. But a review never replaces testing with real users.

say: For example, Aisha reviews the sign-up screen of a savings and loan app for market traders.
The grey text is hard to read. The labels vanish when you type. Contacts access is pre-ticked, and interest and fees appear only after the user accepts.

panel.heading: Making a loan app screen honest

say: She darkens the text to pass the 4.5 to 1 contrast minimum, adds visible labels, unticks the box and explains why the app asks.
Most important for money, she shows the total repayment before acceptance. Hidden costs and pre-ticked boxes are deceptive patterns. They destroy trust.

panel.heading: Making a loan app screen honest

say: Accessibility helps everyone: an older aunt, a mother holding a baby, someone in bright sunshine. Pair every icon with a word.

panel.heading: Design for the women who use it

cards.d: Short common words, icons with text labels, and voice help like WhatsApp voice notes.
Test whether key labels need Pidgin, Hausa, Igbo or Yoruba. English alone may not be enough.
Small images, no auto-play video, nothing sensitive on the lock screen, easy log out.

say: Never assume English alone is enough. Test your key labels.

say: Many users share a phone and pay for data. Make the core task work on a small, older Android screen, and ask only for the data you truly need.

say: Testing with about 5 users shows most of the problems. Blessing gives 5 customers a real scenario and asks them to think aloud. Only 3 of 5 book without help, and 4 of 5 miss the deposit amount.

panel.heading: Blessing's two test rounds

say: She shows the deposit earlier and makes Confirm larger, then tests 5 new customers. All 5 succeed, the time roughly halves, and the System Usability Scale score rises from 58 to 77.

panel.heading: Blessing's two test rounds

say: Say, you want braids this Saturday morning, book a time. Never say, tap Book.
If she asks what to press, reply: what would you do if I were not here? And write 4 of 5 participants, never 80 percent of users. Small tests show problems, not proof.

panel.heading: How to run a fair test
items: Repeat your consent script
Give a goal, not button instructions
Ask her to think aloud
Do not explain or rescue too quickly
Note hesitations, taps, words, success

say: To remember. Review first and fix the worst problems. Make it readable and honest. Then test with 5 users, fix, and test again, measuring success, time, errors and SUS.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Review with the 10 heuristics; rate severity 0 to 4
Contrast 4.5:1, visible labels, never colour alone
No hidden costs or pre-ticked boxes
Test with 5, fix the worst, test again
Measure success, time, errors and SUS
